classification.difficultyReason: Complete the relevant dependent-event probabilities and add the two possible orders for different centres.

content.prompt:
A box has 8 chocolates. 3 have peppermint centres (P) and 5 have caramel centres (C).

Kim randomly chooses a chocolate from the box and eats it.

Sam then randomly chooses and eats one of the remaining chocolates.

A partially completed probability tree is shown.

What is the probability that Kim and Sam choose chocolates with different centres?

spec.description: Two-stage tree with first-stage P above C; each outcome branches to P above C. Ordinary source strokes and labels use house black, with no shading.
spec.mathematics: First-stage probabilities are P: 3/8 and C: 5/8. All four second-stage branches remain unlabelled in the question.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied first-stage probabilities are visible; second-stage probabilities and the final answer appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
Different centres occur along paths PC and CP. After the first chocolate is eaten, 7 remain.

$$\begin{align*}P(PC)&=\frac{3}{8}\times\frac{5}{7}=\frac{15}{56}\\P(CP)&=\frac{5}{8}\times\frac{3}{7}=\frac{15}{56}\\P(\text{different centres})&=\frac{15}{56}+\frac{15}{56}=\frac{15}{28}\end{align*}$$
